question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered, immutable configuration layers as a supported core Gateway startup contract?
rationale: The PR introduces a documented CLI mode with new validation, migration, reload, and persistence semantics for hosted deployments; the open RFC and `maintainer` label show that permanent ownership belongs to maintainers rather than code review automation.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
options.body: Accept the startup-only, read-only design after the write guard is owner/path-scoped and refreshed integration proof passes.

options.title: Keep composition host-owned
options.body: Require Lobster or other launchers to materialize one canonical OpenClaw config outside core and leave the CLI surface unchanged.

options.title: Continue RFC design work
options.body: Pause this implementation until provenance, migration ownership, and managed-host lifecycle boundaries are settled in the RFC.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the startup-only, read-only design after the write guard is owner/path-scoped and refreshed integration proof passes.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows the broadest merger and follow-up ownership across both config persistence and Gateway startup surfaces.
